insight.title: Why Do Prices Change Every Day?
insight.subtitle: A look at the invisible forces that balance our global markets.

sections.text: Imagine a world where everything you buy is controlled by a simple balance. When a product is rare, its value naturally climbs because many people want a small amount of goods. This is called supply. If a harvest fails or a factory stops, there is less to go around, and prices rise quickly.

On the other side, we have demand, which measures how much people want something. If a new toy becomes famous, everyone rushes to buy it. Even if there are many toys available, the high interest allows sellers to charge more. When interest fades, prices drop to encourage people to keep buying.

These two forces work together like a scale to find a fair price. When supply and demand are equal, prices stay steady. This invisible dance happens every second in every store across the globe. Understanding this simple rule helps you see why the cost of your favorite coffee or phone constantly changes.
